title: Close and record earlier jobs landed inside a later job's merge
summary: When a later job's PR merges and its landed content already contains an earlier job's commit (the later job was cut on top of it), Athena should record the earlier job as landed by that merge and close its open PR. Audience: the maintainer who runs `athena land --pr` and reviews PRs.

defaults_applied.how: Tests for each new behavior; cargo test and clippy pass.
Criteria assert landed state and the close call happening.
Handled at the merge-observation point for any contained earlier job, not just the named PRs.
One focused change in the post-merge path of land_pr.
Behavior criteria name cargo test commands.
Criteria check end state rather than wiring.
Docs and comments written for outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Detection: after a job's PR is observed merged (Landed) in land_pr in crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs, find other jobs that have an Open PR link in the state dir and whose landed commit is an ancestor of the merging job's landed commit (the later job was cut on top of it).
Recording: the earlier job's PrLink is set to LinkState::Landed with merged_commit = the later merge's commit, reusing the path a normally merged job takes.

Closing: a new PrHost method (close_pr via the gh client) closes the earlier PR with a comment naming the later PR; a close failure is shown as a warning and never undoes the recorded landing (as with the Pages watch).
Only PRs of jobs provably contained (ancestor check) are touched; unrelated or ambiguous open PRs are left alone.
No governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) need to change.
Tests use the existing fake hosts and temp git repos.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test builds job B on top of job A's landed commit, both with open PR links, merges B's PR via a fake host, and shows A's link becomes Landed with merged_commit equal to B's merge commit and the fake host got exactly one close call for A's PR number. Run `cargo test`.
A test shows an open PR whose job's landed commit is not an ancestor of the merged job's landed commit is neither recorded nor closed. Run `cargo test`.
A test shows that when the host close call fails, the earlier job stays recorded as landed and the failure is a warning, not an error. Run `cargo test`.
`cargo clippy` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
The PrHost trait gains a close-pull-request operation implemented for GhClient and all existing fake hosts; the closing comment names the PR (#N) that contains the content.
gh.rs module docs (and docs/design/native-pr-landing.md if it covers post-merge behavior) describe the supersede-and-close rule and its ancestry condition.
Tests assert the end state (earlier job landed, earlier PR closed once), not merely that a method or trait exists.

out_of_scope: Preventing the stacking at dispatch time.
Changing merge methods or the squash/resync rebuild logic beyond what is needed.
Closing PRs not created by Athena or whose job is not provably contained in the merge.
Editing records/ by hand or any governance configuration.
departures: Cost and time raised slightly: needs a new host trait method, updates to fakes, and a cross-job lookup of PR links.
